chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Usama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Singing is the nest of hypocrisy.

key_terms.النِّفَاقُ: Hypocrisy, specifically the discrepancy between outward appearance and inward belief
key_terms.الْغِنَاءُ: Singing or vocal music, distinct from simple recitation
key_terms.عُشُّ: Nest, denoting a place of origin, dwelling, or accumulation

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of singing in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies singing (al-ghina') as the 'nest of hypocrisy' (ushsh al-nifaq), a metaphor suggesting that it serves as the primary dwelling place where the seeds of insincerity take root within the heart. This narration highlights the spiritual danger of al-ghina' not merely as a musical act, but as a catalyst that erodes inner truthfulness, leading to a disconnect between one's outward appearance and inner faith.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abu Jameela, from Abu Asma,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘The singing is a nest for the hypocrisy’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ali from abu Jamilah from abu ‘Usamah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Music (and singing) is the nest of hypocrisy.’”
